item.question: Lali faces the rising Sun on the school ground. She then turns to face the direction her left hand was pointing to. Which direction is she facing now, and which direction is behind her?
steps: Lali faces the rising Sun. The rising Sun is in the east, so she faces east.
Facing east, her left hand points north and her right hand points south.
She turns to face the direction her left hand was pointing to. That is north, so she now faces north.
Behind her is the opposite of north. North and south are opposite directions, so south is behind her.
Check: north is at the top of the compass rose and south is at the bottom, so they are opposite directions.
item.answer: She is facing north, and south is behind her

item.question: A cycle drives north along a road and turns left at a junction. Which direction is it driving after the turn? At the next junction it turns left again. Which direction is it driving now?
steps: The cycle drives north. Face north: your left hand points west and your right hand points east.
A left turn is a turn towards the left hand. The left hand points west, so after the first turn the cycle drives west.
Now the cycle drives west. Face west: your left hand points south.
The second left turn is towards south, so the cycle now drives south.
Check with the rule: a left turn takes north to west, and west to south.
The two left turns together made the cycle drive the opposite way to the way it started: it started north and now drives south.
item.answer: After the first left turn the cycle drives west. After the second left turn it drives south

Route 2 has two legs, 3 cm north and 4 cm east. Length: 3 + 4 = 7 cm.

Check: the berry is 4 cm east and 3 cm north, and 4 + 3 = 7. A route that goes only east and north cannot be shorter than 7 cm.
item.answer: Routes 1 and 2 are 7 cm and are the shortest. Route 3 is 9 cm, because it goes 1 cm the wrong way
